title: PETA Marketing & Social Media Achievements
subtitle: Pioneering visual-first social strategy, viral video campaigns, and award-winning content for a global nonprofit
seo_title: Viral Social Strategy at PETA — Billions of Impressions
seo_description: A decade pioneering visual-first social media strategy at PETA — viral campaigns, award-winning videos, and culture-shifting content reaching billions of viewers.

flow.text: Social Strategy & Production

In 2011, I began my career in social media on a two-person team: my mentor Helena Soh, and myself. Helena took the time to teach me copywriting excellence. I brought an expertise in visual storytelling to our efforts.

Together, we left a lasting impression on the history of the organization, influenced the lifestyle choices of literal billions of people, and pioneered strategies that later became industry standards.
Our First Viral Moments

Those who work in marketing know that part of the job is learning and keeping up with the forever changing technology, and this was a rapidly evolving era for social media. It wasn't unheard of for companies to produce graphics with text and imagery, but they were working with long turnaround.

Helena and I knew the nature of social media was its pace, that was part of what kept us so passionate, so when I brought my personal Mac in for the first time looking to edit some images off of the corporate Lenovo Thinkpads so that we could actually get some work done, it was fairly natural to start making images as quickly as one of us had an idea. It was then that we became the first brand on Facebook designing effective graphics on the fly.
Viral UGGs Image in Tweet Published in YahooNews

flow.alt: PETA viral UGGs image juxtaposing the boots with the abused animal behind them, picked up by YahooNews

items: The strategy — Think 'visual-first'; workshop a 'sharable' tagline; sharable = what is the user saying when they share it to their profile; help them skip a caption by putting that right on the image; follow the 'gut punch' rule; gut punch = only post if it causes you to audibly gasp (or laugh, etc.); perfect a ~1 sentence post copy until punchy; stay culturally relevant; this was easy because we were cool hipsters.
The results — The juxtaposition of the footwear and the abused animal hit hard; users were angry and sad, which creates sharing and engagement; UGGs were peak popularity, so it felt so relatable.

Big picture — This success taught me the term 'earned media'; 'Viral' was new to social; we only recently got shared news feeds; users didn't hesitate to engage when emotional; YahooNews recognized the novelty, which was an obvious story.

Our new reputation — Digital media outlets saw that piggybacking our work gave them reach; we took down PETA's website on a regular basis because of viral traffic; Facebook, once difficult to get a response from, began requesting meetings; King of website content, BuzzFeed, wanted in on our social game; we worked with BuzzFeed trading strategy in a handful of meetings.

flow.text: Witty Superbowl Tweet Goes Viral

flow.alt: PETA's Super Bowl tweet pairing a caged fur-farm raccoon dog with 'NOT YOURS TO WEAR' aimed at Joe Namath's fur coat

flow.html:
Dear @RealJoeNamath,

The fur on your massive coat was meant for ANIMALS :(

Please consider FAUX! #SuperBowl pic.twitter.com/63TNxttgg8

— PETA (@peta) February 2, 2014
flow.alt: PETA's viral Super Bowl tweet directed at Joe Namath about his fur coat

items: Why live coverage — The goal is to insert our message into real-time, national conversations; this opportunity was otherwise fairly rare; Helena had red carpet event experience from social media at E!; we thrived in face paced environments; finding images was easy as I was discovering my visual encyclopedic memory catalog.

Our process — Spit-balling ideas was our natural dynamic; laptops open, big screen on, and constant coffee and chatter; bring in assistants to help make sure we don't miss opportunities; snacks are essential for keeping energy levels high; possible opportunity found, Helena starts drafting Tweet-length messages; watching her thinking, I gathered the strongest images that gut-checked me.

Opportunity arises — Helena spotted Joe Namath, in a giant, white fur coat, waltzing onto the field; I explored fur farm images for the most emotional gut check I could find; with a few options selected, Helena started paring them with copy; we never publish until it feels done, always opting for quality over quantity.

Why it worked — We chose a technically beautiful photograph of terrified, caged, fur farm raccoon dog; adding the text 'NOT YOURS TO WEAR' created a haunting emotion; dual meaning in the tagline, first the raccoon dog speaking to the viewer; secondary tagline meaning was a direct statement AT Joe Namath; users re-sharing this image were doing it to evoke one of those meanings if not both; users share to build their online identity, tapping us into a bit of virtue signaling; viral status was all but guaranteed, but we had backup; our correspondents who chatted with users and influencers tapped celebrities; sharing the image at a big account with a personalized message asking they share works well; 'Brand Dot Com' was the first online outlet to publish the image; we gave outlets an entry point into the conversation.

flow.alt: Press coverage of PETA's Super Bowl tweet going viral across digital outlets

flow.text: The Same But Different
It wasn't long before Facebook advanced from photo sharing to video sharing. Our tactics were the exact same: Be the first brand to edit videos on the fly, creating and posting three or more a day.

Video was a breakout moment, garnering massive reach. Our bar, or goal, for a solid post quickly was in the millions of impressions per post. This grabbed the attention of colleagues around the globe.

We were officially recognized internally for our consistent, staggeringly successful audience growth when our yearly budget was increased tenfold. This was used to grow our team along with our audience. We upgraded our hardware and started hiring assistants, strategists, and in time, an entire video department specifically for social media videos.
Leveraging Engagement To Influence Culture

It didn't take long to come up with a strategy to flex our newly established audience-base muscles. It was clear we had enough of an audience to generate media attention levels of engagement. Now the strategy could be pushed deeper, potentially dictating the terms of anyone's conversation.
Hijacking the #AskSeaWorld Online Campaign

flow.alt: PETA's #AskSeaWorld tweet featuring orca Tilikum turning SeaWorld's campaign back on itself

flow.html:
Dear #SeaWorld,

Tilikum has a question for you too.#AskSeaWorld pic.twitter.com/3YkEjBuMFO

— PETA (@peta) March 27, 2015
flow.alt: PETA's #AskSeaWorld tweet asking Tilikum's question on behalf of orcas

items: Lessons in thinking critically — SeaWorld, a target of the organization, might not have seen our rapid audience growth; that said, they knew we responded no matter what they posted; it isn't clear what they expected when they launched a campaign soliciting questions; they knew very well that we had a LOT of questions for them, that we posted almost daily; with declining attendance, perhaps they were desperate; or perhaps they paid a consultant and didn't think twice; either way, they wanted the internet to #AskSeaWorld; luckily for orcas, we were able to tell the internet exactly what to #AskSeaWorld.

flow.alt: Stills from PETA's satirical #AskSeaWorld response video featuring actor 'Laura, Fish Doctor And Stuff'

items: We went hard — It isn't often your rival basically creates the campaign against themselves for us; we needed a strategy that took advantage of this once-in-a-career misstep; our new video labs department rapidly produced a satirical video; the video resembled a SeaWorld commercial with comical accuracy; the actor, 'Laura', a 'Fish Doctor And Stuff' had #AskSeaWorld answers for everyone.

We got loud — Campaigns and action team joined the social team in recruiting supporters to #AskSeaWorld; we created powerful graphics and made them readily available online and sent out in emails; the strategy is always the same for conversions: find and amplify that emotional gut check; in just hours, our massive audience bombarded SeaWorld beyond anything they could manage; calling out a problematic company straight to their face was exactly what our audience wanted.

flow.alt: Press coverage of PETA's #AskSeaWorld hijack from Refinery 29 and AdWeek announcing SeaWorld's campaign as a backfire

items: Results poured in — News outlets started announcing SeaWorld's campaign a failure without us needing to ask; they were covering our movement, not SeaWorld's intended message; it was literally impossible to find any of SeaWorld's propaganda under #AskSeaWorld; Refinery 29 posted that 'SeaWorld's #AskSeaWorld Twitter Campaign Backfired Massively'; business publications shared the PR failure and our organization's success; AdWeek chimed in with 'PETA Pokes Fun at Ongoing SeaWorld PR Campaign'.

Culture defining implications — With coordination and powerful content, the power of our impact reached a new level; celebrities, influencers, even moms and dads in middle America took note; 'Oh, no you don't want to anger PETA' reality TV show characters joked; Kanye rapped 'Someone tell PETA my mink is draggin' on the floor'; and again, he rapped 'PETA's mad cause I made a jacket outta possum'; 'Beat the pussy up call PETA' rapped Doja Cat in 'Tia & Tamara'; and again, she rapped 'hit up P.E.T.A., paint on me make me gorgeous'; followed by 'take the geese and chinchilla coat on a walk-in'; a 'walk in' is what we called it when celebrities came to the office for a tour; and of course PETA was well known for their stunning body paint protests; the list goes on with Nicki Minaj, 'Too high to give a shit about PETA'; once a household name, now we were something more, something deeper and cultural and savage; and that is exactly what PETA wanted.

flow.text: #1 Engagement Rate Across Industries

The tactical use of our online audience didn't just craft American culture, next we started getting industry recognition. PRNews Pro might have found earlier reasons to write about our success over these years, but they chose their moment well.

They reached out to interview Helena about our strategy after a video about a baby monkey rescued from animal testing, which come with some rather intense visuals, broke engagement rate records for a few months.

flow.alt: PRNews Pro headline ranking PETA #1 among nonprofits on Facebook for Q3 engagement

items: Beating industry benchmarks — PRNews Pro covered our extremely high engagement rate; they compared us favorably to other organizations; the article highlighted our pioneering approaches for leveraging social media for activism; they featured our Animal Testing rescue video story as an example; the article was headlined with 'PETA, Animal Rights Groups Lead Nonprofits on Facebook During Q3 as Video Engagement Soars'.

It gets personal — They went a step further in their coverage, contacting us to interview Helena; she was Social Director by then, it was quite the honor; in the article they detailed stats and benchmarks for our work.

flow.alt: PRNews Pro interview with Helena Soh detailing PETA's social strategy and engagement benchmarks

items: How we did it — The strategies highlighted through this portfolio are direct results of Helena and my collaboration; our work came from passion, and we were well known for being able to tap into emotion; we pioneered rapid video content creation ahead of market adoption; the productions we put out were always emotionally resonant and shareable by design; content was always optimized for each specific platform; we often coordinated direct marketing emails and SMS pushes to amplify messaging.
Important numbers — The 'Britches' story resulted in 4.5M consumer actions; we achieved a 15% YoY engagement increase; the overall campaign reached over a 61% video engagement rate.

flow.alt: Engagement benchmarks chart showing PETA's industry-leading Q3 social performance

flow.text: These new milestones continued to allow our roles to shift. I was promoted to Marketing Innovations Assistant Manager, a highly autonomous role that involved using data and reporting to find areas of the organization where I could make the biggest impact.

I also hired my own remote and in-office team of correspondents, overseeing their work artfully replying to every comment we got on social media, often getting the more outspoken of trolls to come around to our side and even become polite. They spoke with literally thousands of people a day, as well as working closely with celebrity and influencer campaign planning efforts.

This shift also involved consulting on strategy and giving tutorials on creative production to the marketing teams of the organization's newly opened affiliate offices. I worked closely with employees in India, Australia, London, and Germany.
Strategic Architect & Operational Lead

Helena's and my hands had started to reach in every department of the global organization with a lofty task of shifting the entire organization's strategy from a traditional-communications model to a social-first model. Process had to be broken down and rebuilt, and we needed to remain assertive and confident through constant challenges and resistance.

While leadership insulated the team from institutional friction, I owned the data, built the logic models that defended our strategy, and systematically trained global affiliates to build campaigns from the digital asset outward.
Our end goal for the many departments that all focused on different, highly specialized content, was: Think social-first. Think visual-first.
Award Winning Viral Video Campaigns

In my original social marketing department my role was a bit removed and elevated: I was now routed on all digital content, where I quickly developed a reputation for offering lengthy, logical, highly-detailed feedback that transformed entire video cuts, optimizing them properly for social media — something our traditional production teams were less accustomed to, and part of our new organization-wide endeavor. It required sharing the reputation-backed logic behind every decision we offered across the departments.
Cursing Vegan Grandma Is 'Funny For Good'

flow.alt: Animated still of PETA's 'Tofucken' campaign starring a foul-mouthed vegan grandma preparing the holiday roast

items: Humor has another moment — With such emotional content, it is rare enough that we produce humor, and this went viral; vegan cursing granny was our viral 'Funny For Good' NTEN Do Gooder Award Finalist; called Tofucken the campaign video starred a foul-mouthed, heartwarming grandma making a vegan holiday roast; another organization-wide strategy shift success, as this campaign was built around the video.
Cursing Granny's stats — Tofucken garnered over 100 million video views; today that number is over a billion; this same year we had 1.1 billion Facebook Page impressions.

flow.text: Graphic Horror For Luxury Shoppers

flow.alt: Animated still of PETA's 'Beyond Words' campaign — shoppers horrified to find blood and organs inside luxury leather goods

items: Putting guts in shoppers purses — In this video spot we reminded shoppers that their luxury leather was alive; the video won 1st Place NTEN Do Gooder 'Funny For Good' Award; it was also a ShortyAwards Social Good Finalist.

Bloody heart still in purse — The video was really all about the reactions of the shoppers; as they walked around the store they found blood, tissue, and even organs in all the leather goods; titled 'Beyond Words,' the short was considered comedic and lighthearted; once again, the social-optimized video was the center of this campaign.

flow.alt: Press and awards coverage for PETA's 'Beyond Words' luxury leather campaign

items: The numbers are in — More than 40 million views when the video was submitted; the campaign created a powerful in-store experience; that environment and those reactions made for viral success without any need for dialog; the innovative social optimized strategy created widespread engagement and press coverage.

flow.alt: Additional press features for the 'Beyond Words' campaign and PETA's video department

flow.text: These viral campaigns demonstrate the power of strategic content development and innovative distribution approaches.
When you break it down though, it is really always the same, simple formula. Gut checks create conversions. I applied this in every area of my work for my entire career.
Marketing Innovations & Performance Optimization
Find Ways To Improve Anyone's Work

My job had truly become a game of finding areas where I could have the most impact and improve the organization's work. It was freeing, endlessly creative, and sort of perfect for my personality and way of thinking. I'm down to help anyone in any department, and so I did!

To find opportunities I gathered the entire marketing department's analytics into a single report, distributed as a resource to every branch of the organization worldwide. Then I ran optimization split-testing to improve conversions and social advertising spend and various email metrics, as well as providing strategic insights and recommendations to teams across the organization.
Mobile App Optimization
My data-driven knowhow was particularly helpful in working with our in-house, agency, and freelance iOS app developers and graphic designers.

items: PETA's Direct Action iOS App — Increased conversion rate by 22% month-over-month; broke 1M+ downloads; achieved millions of actions taken; maintained above a 4.8 app store rating with 1.3k reviews.

flow.alt: Screens from PETA's Direct Action iOS App — action feed and campaign detail views

items: iOS Messages Sticker App — Marketing design lead, worked closely with in-house development team; managed beta testing programs; TestFlight; managed press release and launch communications.

flow.alt: PETA's iOS Messages Sticker App pack — animal-themed stickers in conversation

items: Cruelty-Free Product Database iOS App — Bunny Free App was updated every single day; I relayed fine details between the communications and corporate advocacy departments; I worked closely with the contracted developer; optimization and feature updates had great results; we saw increases in return users (+33.7%) and daily page views (+12%).

flow.alt: Bunny Free app screens — cruelty-free product database search and detail views

flow.text: Game Development Strategy Improvements

Heavy copywriting experience and visual storytelling skills translated from social media growth to consulting with agency game developers on content and strategy for our advocacy education game, Kitten Squad.

flow.alt: Kitten Squad mobile game key art — PETA's advocacy education game

items: Playstation-born — I coordinated the iOS and Android launch through marketing; handled communication and writing press releases for launch; executed the cross-media marketing campaigns; reached 1M+ download goal.

flow.alt: Animated Kitten Squad gameplay loop showing UX improvements applied during strategy consulting

items: Consulting for an agency — I got to work closely with the development team of the agency that handled our game development; I reviewed game assets to re-imagine the conversational flow; updated the copywriting in the game; improved the emotionality of the visuals; work helped make the game more accessible and engaging; contributed to a +40% increase in user engagement; maintained focus on the core advocacy education messaging.

flow.alt: Kitten Squad screens — updated dialog flow, refreshed copywriting, and improved emotional visuals

items: This one is for the users — Specifically addressed UX strategy; reviewed user feedback and addressed it head-on; integrated insights into actionable UI writing; produced strategy-development directives; updates resulted in improving completion to 85%; user satisfaction increased to 88%.
